# Why can a position-controlled robot not execute a desired torque from WBC/TSID directly?

> **Current answer:** Desired torque is an upper-level dynamics result. High-ratio position-controlled joints still need calibrated sensing and inverse-dynamics estimation, platform identification, and bounded position offsets to map that torque into a validated actuator interface. HRP-2 identification cannot be copied to another robot or treated as equivalent to joint torque sensing.

## Key terms

- Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU, 惯性测量单元)
- Inverse Dynamics (逆动力学)
- Joint Torque (关节力矩)
- Task-Space Inverse Dynamics (TSID, 任务空间逆动力学)
- Whole-Body Control (WBC, 全身控制)
- Position Control (位置控制)

## Applicable robots

- HRP-2 in the paper; other position-controlled robots require independent identification

## Applicable simulators

- Rigid-body dynamics models used for estimator and upper-level controller validation

## Controllers and methods

- Task-space inverse dynamics
- Position-offset torque-oriented control

## Applicable environments

- Model-based humanoid control on high-ratio position-controlled joints

## Assumptions

- External wrench sensing, IMU, and inertial model are calibrated for torque estimation.
- The position-servo actuator map is identified and monitored over direction, speed, and temperature.

- First verify the applicable robot, simulator, controller, environment, and assumptions, then follow the evidence locators below to inspect the original experiment or implementation.

## Result

- Desired torque is an upper-level dynamics result. High-ratio position-controlled joints still need calibrated sensing and inverse-dynamics estimation, platform identification, and bounded position offsets to map that torque into a validated actuator interface. HRP-2 identification cannot be copied to another robot or treated as equivalent to joint torque sensing.

## Limitations

- External wrench sensing, IMU, and inertial model are calibrated for torque estimation.
- The position-servo actuator map is identified and monitored over direction, speed, and temperature.
